about.tagline: A hardware profiler for Linux. What CPU-Z, GPU-Z and HWMonitor do on Windows, in one native program: what machine you have and what it is doing right now.

bench.card.title: Benchmark
bench.compare.title: Previous runs on this machine   ·   {signo}{pct}% against the one from {fecha}
bench.cond.endfreq.tip: The average over the last stretch. If it is well below the peak, the processor did not hold its top clock through the run.
bench.cond.load.tip: What was keeping the machine busy right before starting. With background load the result cannot be compared.

bench.dialog.duration.body:
How many minutes each of the ten measurements lasts.

bench.dialog.name: Name of the run
bench.dialog.name.body: So you remember what changed between one and the next:
bench.dialog.name.tip: Give it a name: «new thermal paste», «summer»…
bench.drift.cooler: This run peaked {grados} °C below the median of the {n} previous {pruebas} with the same score. If you have just cleaned it or repasted it, this is where it shows.
bench.drift.hotter: This run peaked {grados} °C above the median of the {n} previous {pruebas} with the same score. That is usually dust or dried-out thermal paste — or simply a warmer room, which no sensor in the machine measures.
bench.duration.tip:
How long each of the ten measurements lasts: five loads, on one thread and on all of them. The whole run takes ten times this.

Longer ones do not give a higher score: they give the one that holds up once the machine is already warm.
bench.explain.scaling:
Scaling
How much performance multiplies when using every thread. It never reaches the thread count: the ones sharing a core split the same execution units.
bench.history.note: Only from this machine and only on disk: nothing is sent anywhere. Comparing against numbers off the internet hardly ever helps, because they were measured with another governor and another temperature; comparing against yourself does tell you whether something changed.
bench.intro: Measures the processor with five different loads, first on one thread and then on all of them. The interesting part is not just the number: each load scales differently, and that shows what makes use of the threads and what sits waiting on memory. While it runs, the machine goes flat out.
bench.quick.tip: Eight seconds instead of twenty. Enough to get an idea, but with less room for the turbo to settle.
board.card.title: Motherboard
board.tip.bios: The «System BIOS Release» field of the SMBIOS table. Not the version the maker publishes on its site, but the one the firmware declares about itself.
board.tip.chipset: The full name pci.ids uses for the LPC/eSPI bridge on bus 0, which is what acts as the chipset.
board.tip.memctl: On modern processors it is built into the CPU itself, not the chipset.
cache.l3.uneven: The L3 is not the same across the processor: {reparto}.
cache.l3.vcache: That is the V-Cache stacked on just one of the two chiplets: a thread that lands on the big one gets more out of memory.
caches.line.note: The smallest unit that travels between memory and cache. Reading a single byte pulls in the whole line, which is why walking contiguous data is far faster than jumping around memory.
caches.map.note: Each block is one physical cache instance; its width is the logical CPUs that share it.
caches.subtitle: {n} distinct caches over {nucleos} cores and {hilos} threads
caches.ways.note: An N-way cache stores each address in one of N possible places. More ways reduce clashes between data competing for the same set, at the cost of a more expensive lookup.
clock.turbo.capped: The kernel caps it at {actual} of the {max} the silicon can do
clock.turbo.off: Turbo is off: the silicon would reach {max}
core.name: core {n}
core.spread: the weakest one (core {n}) tops out at {pct}% of the best
core.spread.type: the weakest one (core {n}) tops out at {pct}% of the best of its kind
cpu.stars.note: : the ones that came out best of the wafer according to the firmware, and where the scheduler sends single-threaded work.
disk.warn.backup: the power-loss backup memory has failed
disk.warn.life: It has {pct}% of its life left, by its own wear counter.
disk.warn.media.many: {n} pieces of data that could not be read since it left the factory.
disk.warn.media.one: {n} piece of data that could not be read since it left the factory.
disk.warn.pmr: its persistent memory region is unreliable
disk.warn.readonly: it has switched to read-only mode
disk.warn.reliability: the drive has downgraded its own reliability
disk.warn.spare: the spare area has dropped below the maker's threshold
disk.warn.temp: the temperature is outside the range it accepts
disk.warn.unknown: The drive is flagging a problem (code {codigo}).
gpu.codec.name: Codec
gpu.engine.name: Engine
home.tagline: What hardware you have inside and what it is doing right now. Everything is read from the system itself: no data leaves this machine.
mem.channel.same: All {n} modules sit on the same channel. Split across two, the memory would move twice as much per second.
mem.channel.single: There is only one module, so memory runs at half its bandwidth. A matching second module in the other channel doubles it; on a machine with integrated graphics that shows up in the frame rate more than almost anything else.
mem.modules.read.many: {n} modules read from their SPD chips{vel}
mem.modules.read.one: {n} module read from its SPD chip{vel}
mem.spd.needsperm: · the slot and the capacity need permissions
mem.title: {tam} of memory
mem.underclocked: The memory runs at {actual} MT/s of the {rated} it claims to support. That is usually the fast profile —XMP or EXPO— left off in the BIOS, though it can also be the processor's official limit.
memory.spd.note: The SPD is a chip every module carries with its own specifications. It says what speed it can run at, while the BIOS decides the one it actually runs at: without XMP enabled it stays on JEDEC's conservative values.
net.none.body: No interface has a route to the network.
net.units.note: The same traffic is either 116 MB/s or 931 Mb/s: speed tests use bits.
note.hardware: This machine does not expose it
note.platform: Does not apply to this platform
pcie.now: Running at {actual}; the card and the slot can do {max}

settings.accent.help: The colour used to highlight values, charts and the open section.
settings.accent.label: Accent colour
settings.allflags.help: By default only the flags that matter are listed. Turned on, all 53 that CPUID reports on this machine show up.
settings.allflags.label: Show every instruction set
settings.density.help: Spacious leaves more room between rows and columns; compact tightens things up to fit more on the same screen.
settings.density.label: Density
settings.fluid.help: Lines glide instead of jumping. It changes no reading at all: it just redraws more often, and costs 2% of one core. Press space to freeze what is on screen.
settings.fluid.label: Smooth chart motion
settings.fontsize.help: Scales up every bit of text. Cards and columns grow with it so nothing gets clipped.
settings.fontsize.label: Text size
settings.interval.help: Every reading walks sysfs and hwmon. Below half a second the cost starts to show; above two, the charts lose detail.
settings.interval.label: Refresh every
settings.language.help: Spanish is the original: when a phrase has not been translated yet, it shows in Spanish rather than blank.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.netunit.help: The same traffic is either 116 MB/s or 931 Mb/s. Speed tests and providers use bits; download managers use bytes.
settings.netunit.label: Network speed
settings.report.button: Save a report of this machine…
settings.tempunit.label: Temperature unit
settings.theme.label: Theme
storage.health.body: Power-on hours, terabytes written and wear are kept by each drive in its own diagnostic counters. The kernel reserves those commands for the administrator because they are the same ones used to erase a drive.
storage.health.hint: The helper that gets launched only knows how to ask for diagnostics and read a few system tables: it runs no commands and writes nothing.
storage.health.read: Diagnostics read from {n} of {total} drives. The rest do not publish them or did not answer.
storage.subtitle: {tam} used across {n} mounted partitions
storage.title: {tam} across {n} drives
storage.warn.hint: The drive itself says so in its diagnostic log. Worth having a copy of whatever is inside.
sys.kernel.name: Kernel
sys.subtitle: {equipo} · up {tiempo}
sys.tip.apps: Total minus free, buffers and reclaimable cache. It comes out slightly below «Used» because that one includes what cannot be given back.
sys.tip.cache: Reclaimable disk cache: Cached + SReclaimable − Shmem.
sys.tip.used: Total minus available. Free alone is not subtracted because on Linux the kernel uses every spare byte as cache, and gives it back the moment something asks for it.
throttle.unknown: a reason it does not report
